site.author: Angela St. Cyr
site.about_short: Angela St. Cyr is a home stylist, blogger, and enthusiastic cook based in Vancouver, Canada — one of the most expensive cities in North America. With her two daughters now grown and out in the world of their own, Angela continues to prove that you can live and design the life you want, regardless of budget. Home Stylist, Blogger, Enthusiastic Cook, former participant in the 100-Mile Challenge, and a longtime Jamie Oliver Food Revolution Ambassador.

recipes.title: Sticky Chile Lime Chicken Salad
recipes.description: Sweet, salty, and just enough heat to make your tastebuds hum.

sections.text: I LOVE salads!!! It doesn't matter what time of year, give me an interesting salad with a bold mix of flavours and I'm in! This is one of my all time favourites, it's sweet and salty with just enough heat to get your tastebuds humming. This recipe generously serves 4, allowing for 2 chicken thighs per person.

items: 8 boneless chicken thighs (skin on or off)
1/4 cup olive oil (lime-infused if you can find it)
Pop everything except the chicken into a blender or food processor and pulse until it becomes a smooth sauce.
Remove 1/4 cup of the sauce and set aside — this will be the base for the salad dressing.
Pour the remaining sauce over the chicken and marinate for at least an hour, or up to overnight.

sections.text: While the chicken is marinating, prepare your salad. This is what I like to use, but feel free to swap in anything that suits your taste:

items: 1 tbsp sweet chile sauce (I like Aroy-D)
Whisk everything together in a small bowl.
Season with salt and pepper if needed.
Feel free to add a little more oil or rice vinegar to balance the acidity to your taste.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and cook either in a non-stick skillet or on the barbecue.
Sear one side of the chicken for about 5 minutes.
Flip it over and drizzle 1 tsp of sweet chile sauce over the seared side of each piece.
Cook the other side for 5 minutes, then flip again and drizzle another teaspoon of chile sauce over the second side.
Cook for another few minutes per side until the sauce is sticky and the chicken reads 165°F (75°C) on a meat thermometer.

sections.text: Place the cooked, sliced chicken onto the prepared salad and drizzle with the dressing. This is guaranteed to become a family favourite!

recipes.title: The Ultimate Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.description: My most requested recipe — soft in the middle, crisp on the edges, and packed with chocolate.

sections.text: These are the cookies I bring to every potluck, every school event, every neighbour's housewarming. The secret is a touch more brown sugar than white, and pulling them out a minute or two before they look fully done — they'll set as they cool.

items: In a large bowl, cream together butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then stir in vanilla.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, and salt. Gradually blend into the wet mixture.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake for 10-12 minutes or until golden brown. Let cool on the baking sheet for 2 minutes before transferring.

recipes.tip: This can easily be made gluten-free by using a commercially prepared gluten-free flour blend formulated for baking.

recipes.title: Rustic Tomato Soup
recipes.description: A creamy, deeply flavoured tomato soup that tastes like it simmered all day.

sections.text: There's nothing more comforting than a bowl of really good tomato soup with a grilled cheese on the side. This version uses canned whole tomatoes (better flavour than diced) and gets blended smooth, with just enough cream to make it silky without being heavy.

items: 2 cans (28 oz each) whole peeled tomatoes
Fresh basil, salt, and pepper to taste
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in tomatoes (with juices), broth, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth.
Stir in cream, season with salt and pepper, and garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.tip: For an extra rich flavour, roast the tomatoes in the oven before adding them to the pot.
